13 June 2029, 22.05. Verbatim transcript of the original Turkish audio recording of the statement, before interpretation.

Ayten Yıldız: “It was ten past nine. The noise came from the floor below, from the top of the stairs. Two men. One said ‘Let go of it!’, the other said something, I didn’t understand, it was German. Then something rolled down the stairs.”

Interpreter Selin Aras (in German, on the recording): “The floor below — so the ground floor, yes? The witness lives on the first floor.”

Ayten Yıldız’s reply is not on the recording; the record moves on to the next question.
ORIGINAL AUDIO TRANSCRIPT — AYTEN YILDIZ (TURKISH)

· Cause of death: broken neck from a fall.
· Fresh bruises consistent with fingertips on the outer side of both upper arms; just before the fall.
· Grazes on the knuckles of the right hand: he struck someone or something.
· A fresh fabric fibre and bloodstain on the stair railing, level with the first-floor landing (scene team note).
· Estimated time of death: 21.05 – 21.20.
PRELIMINARY AUTOPSY NOTE
In Turkish, without an interpreter.
I used to see him. Always came for that woman, Lena. They’d hug at the door, talk quietly. If her husband knew, there’d be hell to pay, I thought to myself.
She lowered her voice.
Did you know the young man who died?
I don’t know, dear, I told you what I heard.
On the second floor. I moved upstairs two years ago, my first-floor flat was damp. The management still lists my old place, I’ve told them so many times.
Which floor do you live on?
Ten past nine. From the floor below, at the top of the stairs, two men’s voices. One shouted ‘Let go of it!’ Then a crash, down the stairs.
She squeezed her prayer beads.
What did you hear yesterday evening?
“From the floor below, at the top of the stairs.”

DOOR CAMERA CLOUD RECORD — VOGT FLAT

A correction note was added to the interpretation record: “the floor below” was written down verbatim, alongside the witness’s own floor. bube Berlin made it a rule that relative expressions are passed on without interpretation.
The case was built on the ground floor; Uwe Brandt’s door stayed sealed for weeks.
Ayten Yıldız’s statement was read against her own door; the old woman refused ever to testify again.
The floor could not be established; the defence demolished the witness’s statement entirely.
Lena was questioned and her protected address went into the file. Markus got the address from his lawyer, who read the file.
Markus Vogt was arrested for manslaughter. A week later Lena collected her passport from the evidence store; she didn’t open her brother’s box, and kept it as it was.
The death was closed as an accident. Lena’s passport was lost in a bin lorry; a month later Lena went back home.
Uwe Brandt was taken into custody and released two days later. Markus Vogt learned Lena’s new address from an official notice.

Lena was at the women’s refuge in Wedding that evening; Jonas was there on her behalf.
He left his shift early, the door camera shows him on the landing, and Jonas’s phone and Lena’s passport were in the bin with his prints.
The grip marks on his arms, the blood on the railing and the shout “Let go of it!” point to a struggle.
The argument wasn’t on the ground floor; the interpretation record had turned the witness’s “the floor below” into the wrong floor.

At the women’s refuge.
My passport, my papers, a few things. Markus was on the evening shift, he wouldn’t be back before nine. I gave Jonas my key. It was going to take ten minutes.
She clasped her hands together to stop them shaking.

I can’t talk about that now.
My brother. I was a Keller. The neighbours probably thought he was my lover; he was the one who held me when I cried at the door.
She wiped her eyes.

No. But he knew Jonas knew. ‘Your brother can’t hide you from me,’ he texted yesterday morning.

He was going to call Lena, that’s how I knew. Without the passport she couldn’t leave. …I just didn’t want her to go.

FIRST FLOOR  /  SUSPICIOUS DEATH

An off-duty courier is found dead in the stairwell of an old block of flats in Kreuzberg. A witness heard shouting from the ground floor; the man on the ground floor hates couriers. The witness spoke in Turkish.

On 13 June 2029 at 21.14 in Kreuzberg, a man’s body was found at the bottom of the stairwell of an old block of flats at Lindenhof 9. Beside him, a taped-up cardboard box, handwritten on top: “L.K.”

Deceased: Jonas Keller (29), courier. Not in uniform, off shift.

Patrol note: “Fell down the stairs with a heavy box. An elderly woman on the second floor, a witness, said she heard shouting from the ground floor around 21.10 (statement taken through an interpreter). The ground-floor tenant is known to have rowed with couriers.”

The record said the witness lived on the first floor; they’d taken it from the tenant list. The floor below that is the ground floor. I asked her, I thought she didn’t answer… Wait. What if the list was out of date?

With the interpreter.

Normally verbatim: ‘the floor below’. This time I clarified it, to be clear. The worst mistake is the one made in good faith.

SHIFT RECORD — MARKUS VOGT

The original audio separated the witness’s relative expression from the interpreter’s reading; the witness’s own account showed she lived on the second floor. The door camera’s cloud backup, the shift record and the phone and passport from the bin led to Markus Vogt. The admission note revealed that the courier taken for a “lover” was her brother.
The interpretation of a statement is a reading: go back to the original if you can. Relative words like “the floor below” carry no meaning without knowing where the speaker stands.
Kreuzberg, Lindenhof 9 — June 2029

Lena Vogt fled domestic violence and took shelter in a women’s refuge. Her brother, Jonas Keller, went to fetch her passport and belongings at an hour when Markus Vogt was on shift. Markus had left his shift early; he caught Jonas on the first-floor landing, they struggled over the box and the passport, and Jonas fell down the stairs. Markus threw the phone and the passport in the courtyard bin and deleted the door camera recordings. The witness, Ayten Yıldız, had said “from the floor below”; the interpreter, looking at the old tenant list, wrote it down as “the ground floor”.
Who is responsible for Jonas Keller’s death?
